name: Saturation Anomaly Map
description: Maps saturation anomalies across image regions — AI generators often produce over-saturated or unnaturally uniform saturation.
mechanism:
This method creates spatial maps of color saturation anomalies to detect AI-generated content and image manipulation:

1. **HSV/HSL Saturation Extraction**: The image is converted to the HSV (Hue-Saturation-Value) color space. The saturation channel S = (max(R,G,B) − min(R,G,B)) / max(R,G,B) is extracted at each pixel. A local saturation map is computed by averaging S over blocks of 16×16 pixels. In natural photographs, saturation varies predictably with scene content: shadows have lower saturation (Hunt effect), highlights approach zero saturation (clipping), and specular surfaces show zero saturation.

2. **Saturation-Intensity Relationship Analysis**: In authentic photographs, the relationship between saturation and intensity follows a characteristic bow-shaped curve: low saturation at very low intensities (noise-dominated), increasing through mid-tones, then decreasing at highlights (sensor clipping). The method fits a quadratic model S(V) = a·V² + b·V + c to the saturation-intensity scatter plot. AI-generated images often show: (a) higher overall saturation, (b) more uniform saturation across the intensity range, or (c) saturation that doesn't decrease at highlights because AI generators don't model sensor physics.

3. **Local Saturation Consistency**: The image is divided into overlapping blocks, and each block's mean saturation and saturation variance are computed. In natural images, adjacent blocks sharing similar content should have similar saturation statistics. The method computes the saturation gradient map |∇S| and identifies regions where saturation changes abruptly without corresponding changes in content or lighting. These discontinuities indicate compositing (different source material with different color processing) or AI inpainting (where the generator fails to match the saturation profile of surrounding content).

4. **Gamut Analysis and Out-of-Gamut Detection**: The method analyzes the color gamut occupancy of each region. Natural photographs captured in sRGB rarely achieve maximum saturation at medium-to-high lightness levels due to camera ISP limitations. The method identifies pixels or regions with colors near the sRGB gamut boundary, which can indicate: (a) aggressive saturation boost in post-processing, (b) out-of-gamut colors clamped during color space conversion, or (c) AI-generated content that produces colors outside the natural photographic gamut.
parameters:
Color space: HSV
Block size: 16×16 pixels
Saturation-intensity model: quadratic S(V) = aV² + bV + c
Gradient threshold: |∇S| > 0.2 without content edge
Gamut boundary distance: < 2% of sRGB boundary
Minimum image size: 128×128 pixels
Saturation map smoothing: Gaussian σ = 4 pixels
accuracy: 76–84% accuracy for detecting AI-generated images via saturation analysis. Saturation-intensity curve anomaly detection achieves AUC of 0.82. Local saturation consistency for splicing detection: F1-score of 0.79. Over-saturation in AI portraits is detected with 88% precision. Performance is best on natural scene photographs.
source: Farid, H. (2009). Image Forgery Detection. IEEE Signal Processing Magazine, 26(2), 16–25.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated images with unnatural color saturation profiles. Identifying composited regions with mismatched saturation characteristics. Detecting over-processed or heavily filtered photographs. Analyzing color authenticity for forensic investigation.
strengths:
• Saturation anomalies are perceptible to trained observers and measurable automatically
• Saturation-intensity relationship is physics-grounded (sensor response model)
• Local consistency analysis localizes manipulated regions
• Gamut analysis detects impossible or unlikely color values
• Works across diverse image content types
limitations:
• Artistic photography with intentional saturation adjustments triggers false positives
• HDR images and computational photography produce non-standard saturation profiles
• Modern AI generators produce increasingly natural saturation distributions
• Different camera manufacturers apply different saturation curves in their ISP
• Low-light images have inherently low and noisy saturation, reducing analysis reliability

references.title: Farid, H. — Image Forgery Detection (IEEE Signal Processing Magazine 2009)
